title: Is there any alternatives like `docker buildx imagetools` ?
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/containers/podman/discussions/20972
Originally posted by **abcfy2** December 11, 2023 Hi there. Docker cli has a useful `docker buildx imagetools` could show remote image informations, like supported platforms and sha256. ```sh # docker buildx imagetools inspect python Name: docker.io/library/python:latest MediaType: application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json Digest: sha256:6d7fa2d5653e1d0eb464a672ded01f973e49e4a7ded59703c7bdcf6b92eac736 Manifests: Name: Thanks.

comments.body: Let's discuss in https://github.com/containers/podman/discussions/20972 first whether this should be done.
A friendly reminder that this issue had no activity for 30 days.

Hello! Would love build this feature if no one is else working on it :) 

- Basically you would like two cmds i.e `podman imagetools inspect ...` and `podman imagetools create ...`? Maybe i'll start with `inspect` first? 
- I can grab the data from `skopeo inspect` just like it's been suggesting in the Discussions thread? Do you think i could just exec call skopeo? Or maybe there's a way import skopeo funcs?

Any tips/tricks/suggestions appreciated!

> Hello! Would love build this feature if no one is else working on it :)

Thanks!

>     * Basically you would like two cmds i.e `podman imagetools inspect ...` and `podman imagetools create ...`? Maybe i'll start with `inspect` first?

I leave that up to you :)  `podman image inspect` already exists but it works only on images in the local storage; not with images on a remote registry.

>     * I can grab the data from `skopeo inspect` just like it's been suggesting in the Discussions thread? 

That the depends on the goal we decide on; I don't think we decided that yet.  In my opinion, I don't think it's sustainable to continue chasing Docker or buildkit.  The projects evolve and mature and at some point, Podman should allow itself to diverge.  Podman has achieved feature parity in the past, so I think the goal has been met.

That doesn't mean I would block this work.  But I want to highlight that there are tradeoffs to effectively chase/copy.

> Do you think i could just exec call skopeo? Or maybe there's a way import skopeo funcs?

Skopeo and Podman share the underlying libraries doing all the heavy lifting and work.  In the case of images, the common library lives at https://github.com/containers/image.  You can follow the code paths of `skopeo inspect` to see how a remote image is being inspected.

We have discussed remote scanning of manifest and manifests list for years and have told people to use skopeo. In another PR we discussed shipping skopeo with podman in a podman machine, but right now think it takes up too much space. In my opinion the proper action is to add this ability to Podman.  I think following Docker CLI makes sense if we need and want the feature.

It should be done using containers/image directly rather then execing skopeo.

@rhatdan I agree in spirit.  But part of this conversation here is to mimic Docker/buildkit.  That would imply returning the same data and having to continue chasing down future changes etc.

I am advocating to discuss implementing what we/this community needs.  So we may decide to implement remote inspection but rather than copying Docker, we can just make this part of `podman image inspect`.

FWIW as a regular docker user who is looking to migrate/integrate more podman in local env...I usually just replace `docker` with `podman` and see if the feature I'm looking for is already there. 

In this case i know `buildx` is docker only so i just drop that and just do `podman imagetools inspect python` and see what the cli throws back! 

maybe I'm doing it wrong? let me know what you think!

No makes sense.  Podman has some buildx support, in that `podman build` supports many buildx features.  It even has a hidden feature where `podman buildx build` ends up as `podman build` More advanced features of buildx are not implemented and are not likely unless they become hugely popular.

docker buildx imagetools inspect quay.io/podman/stable
should be something like

podman image inspect --atregistry quay.io/podman/stable

Or something like this.
IMHO, `podman buildx imagetools create $image:$tag -t  $image:$new-tag` as a drop-in replacement as sugested by @pixelsoccupied would be of great value.

I would still like to have this functionality, but it seems that the discussion above fizzled out before anything happened.
In particular it should use `/etc/containers/registries.conf`, which the version of skopeo that comes with Ubuntu 24.04 apparently doesn't do.

I'm on the same boat because komodo has issues due to this bug.

**WARNING WARNING WARNING**

As a temporary hack I instructed gemini or claude (can't remember) to make a wrapper that only solves this issue and only partially. I expect this bug will be solved in the future and then this will not be needed. It's neither a proper solution nor a good one. It's a LLM encoded hack. It works for me, it might not work for you

But remember this is LLM/AI generated. Use it at your own risk! Dont blame me or this project if anything breaks

And also: I understand this kind of solutions are frown upon (and with a reason!) but nontheless here I am

**WARNING WARNING WARNING**

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# docker-imagetools-shim.sh
#
# Purpose:
#   Komodo v2's image-update checker shells out to:
#       docker buildx imagetools inspect <ref> [--raw|--format TEMPLATE]
#   to read the remote registry digest without pulling.
#
#   Under podman-docker, `docker` == `podman`, and podman's `buildx`
#   compat layer does not implement the `imagetools` subcommand at all
#   (see: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/20975,
#   https://github.com/moghtech/komodo/issues/1332). Any invocation dies
#   with "unknown flag: --format" before it ever reaches image logic.
#
#   Fix: intercept ONLY that exact call shape and answer it with
#   `skopeo inspect`, which talks to the registry API directly and needs
#   no buildx/BuildKit at all. Every other docker/podman invocation is
#   passed straight through unmodified.
#
# Install:
#   1. Find where podman-docker actually put its shim:
#        dpkg -L podman-docker 2>/dev/null | grep 'bin/docker'
#      On Debian/Ubuntu this is normally /usr/bin/docker (symlink -> podman).
#      Confirm REAL_DOCKER below matches that path.
#   2. Copy this file to /usr/local/bin/docker (NOT alongside — replacing
#      the name `docker` is the point, since /usr/local/bin precedes
#      /usr/bin in the default PATH systemd units inherit).
#        install -m 0755 docker-imagetools-shim.sh /usr/local/bin/docker
#   3. Ensure `skopeo` and `jq` are installed on this Periphery host:
#        apt install -y skopeo jq          # Debian/Ubuntu
#        dnf install -y skopeo jq          # Fedora/RHEL
#   4. Restart periphery so it re-resolves `docker` on PATH.
#
# Verify BEFORE trusting it against production stacks — run manually as
# the periphery user first:
#        docker buildx imagetools inspect docker.io/library/nginx:latest \
#            --format '{{json .}}' | jq .
# and compare against what a real docker install prints for the same
# image, to confirm the shape matches what your Komodo version expects.
# If Komodo's actual call uses a template shape not handled below, add
# it to the case statement — the digest field alone is what update
# comparison logic cares about in every Komodo version I'm aware of.

set -euo pipefail

# Path to the REAL docker/podman binary — must NOT be this script.
REAL_DOCKER="/usr/bin/docker"

pass_through() {
  exec "$REAL_DOCKER" "$@"
}

# Only intervene for: buildx imagetools inspect <ref> [flags...]
if [[ "${1:-}" == "buildx" && "${2:-}" == "imagetools" && "${3:-}" == "inspect" ]]; then
  shift 3

  ref=""
  raw=0
  fmt=""

  while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
      --raw)
        raw=1
        shift
        ;;
      --format)
        fmt="${2:-}"
        shift 2
        ;;
      --format=*)
        fmt="${1#*=}"
        shift
        ;;
      -*)
        # Unrecognized flag for this subcommand — don't guess, bail to real docker
        # so the original (informative) error is preserved.
        pass_through buildx imagetools inspect "$@"
        ;;
      *)
        ref="$1"
        shift
        ;;
    esac
  done

  if [[ -z "$ref" ]]; then
    echo "docker-imagetools-shim: no image reference given" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  # Normalize bare refs the way docker/podman implicitly do:
  #   nginx            -> docker.io/library/nginx:latest
  #   nginx:1.27        -> docker.io/library/nginx:1.27
  #   myuser/app        -> docker.io/myuser/app:latest
  normalize_ref() {
    local r="$1"
    if [[ "$r" != *"/"* ]]; then
      r="library/${r}"
    fi
    if [[ "$r" != *"."*"/"* && "$r" != *":"*"/"* && "$r" != "localhost/"* ]]; then
      r="docker.io/${r}"
    fi
    if [[ "$r" != *":"* || "$r" == *"/"*":"*"/"* ]]; then
      : # has a tag already or ambiguous — leave alone
    fi
    if [[ "$r" != *"@sha256:"* && "${r##*:}" == "$r" ]]; then
      r="${r}:latest"
    fi
    printf '%s' "$r"
  }
  norm_ref="$(normalize_ref "$ref")"

  if ! command -v skopeo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "docker-imagetools-shim: skopeo not found — install it (apt/dnf install skopeo)" >&2
    exit 1
  fi

  if [[ "$raw" -eq 1 ]]; then
    # docker buildx imagetools inspect --raw prints the raw manifest/index
    # JSON bytes exactly as the registry returns them. skopeo --raw does
    # the same thing.
    exec skopeo inspect --raw "docker://${norm_ref}"
  fi

  # Get the raw manifest once; we build every other output shape from it.
  raw_manifest="$(skopeo inspect --raw "docker://${norm_ref}")"
  media_type="$(printf '%s' "$raw_manifest" | jq -r '.mediaType // .schemaVersion // empty')"

  # Get the digest of the manifest itself (what --format Digest shows).
  top_digest="$(skopeo inspect "docker://${norm_ref}" 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.Digest // empty')"
  if [[ -z "$top_digest" ]]; then
    # Older single-arch images: compute from raw bytes directly.
    top_digest="sha256:$(printf '%s' "$raw_manifest" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  fi

  is_list=0
  if printf '%s' "$media_type" | grep -qiE 'manifest\.list|image\.index'; then
    is_list=1
  fi

  if [[ "$is_list" -eq 1 ]]; then
    # NOTE: norm_ref is passed via --arg, NOT via `env.NORM_REF`. jq's `env`
    # only sees variables actually exported into the process environment —
    # referencing an unset one evaluates to `null`, and `null | split(":")`
    # is a jq type error, which silently fell through to the `|| echo '[]'`
    # fallback below in an earlier version of this script. Verified against
    # a real multi-arch manifest list (nginx:latest) on 2026-09-04.
    manifests_json="$(printf '%s' "$raw_manifest" | jq -c --arg ref "$norm_ref" '
      [.manifests[] | {
        Name: (($ref | split(":")[0] | split("@")[0]) + "@" + .digest),
        Digest: .digest,
        MediaType: .mediaType,
        Platform: ((.platform.os // "unknown") + "/" + (.platform.architecture // "unknown"))
      }]
    ' 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')"
  else
    manifests_json="[]"
  fi

  result_json="$(jq -n \
    --arg name "$norm_ref" \
    --arg mediatype "$media_type" \
    --arg digest "$top_digest" \
    --argjson manifests "$manifests_json" \
    '{Name: $name, MediaType: $mediatype, Digest: $digest, Manifests: $manifests}')"

  case "$fmt" in
    *json*|"")
      # Covers --format '{{json .}}' and bare `--format json`.
      printf '%s\n' "$result_json"
      ;;
    *)
      # Best-effort human-readable fallback matching docker's default text
      # output, for any other template shape we didn't special-case.
      echo "Name:      $norm_ref"
      echo "MediaType: $media_type"
      echo "Digest:    $top_digest"
      if [[ "$manifests_json" != "[]" ]]; then
        echo "Manifests:"
        printf '%s' "$manifests_json" | jq -r '.[] | "  Name: \(.Name)\n  MediaType: \(.MediaType)\n  Platform: \(.Platform)\n"'
      fi
      ;;
  esac

  exit 0
fi

# Anything else: not our concern, hand off untouched.
pass_through "$@"
```

The funny thing is that providing the functionality is super simple, since it already *mostly* exists. 

If you are (like I am in my use case) interested in the image ID (sha256) the answer is already in the output from `podman manifest inspect docker.io/library/python:latest`:
```
$ podman manifest inspect docker.io/library/python:latest
{
    "schemaVersion": 2,
    "mediaType": "application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.list.v2+json",
    "manifests": [
        {
            "mediaType": "application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json",
            "size": 2318,
            "digest": "sha256:779838536f5a0d42d150edbf59fcb08af24fd21b3dd6af7f308dbadcbb6ff3cc",
            "platform": {
                "architecture": "amd64",
                "os": "linux"
            }
        },
...
```
Except if there is only a single image instead of a list. Then you get something like
```
$ podman manifest inspect $IMAGE
Error: parsing manifest blob "{\n  \"schemaVersion\": 2,\n  \"mediaType\": \"application/vnd.oci.image.manifest.v1+json\",\n  \"config\": {\n    \"mediaType\": \"application/vnd.oci.image.config.v1+json\",\n    \"digest\": \"sha256:bce047a89d4308761bf83e0187daa54b14e6a8ea0a8617a6f52bb19ee440c4c1\",\n ....
Treating single images as manifest lists is not implemented
```

The json output from the server is already printed in the error message of `podman manifest inspect`, and if we just want the image ID (sha256), the answer is in there! Unfortunately it is printed with quotes and newlines escaped, embedded into the error message, so it is not valid json...

For a public image where I see this sort of output: `podman manifest inspect docker.io/library/python:2.7.9` which results in triple-escaped quotes for some reason...
